title: Clinical Science Research Core
text: PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT - CLINICAL SCIENCE RESEARCH CORE The Clinical Science Research Core (CSRC) enhances and facilitates leading-edge clinical and translational nutrition/obesity research through the operation of two distinct but interactive sub-cores that provide an array of services and unique training through a cohesive, “one-stop” organizational structure that ensures optimal integration of high-quality services and training. In the last year, the CSRC has made considerable changes in leadership and services in response to investigator request/needs. The Clinical Studies Performance sub- core assists investigators in conducting clinical nutrition/obesity research protocols by providing: i) consultation in designing a clinical research study and in interpreting the results of the data generated by core analyses, ii) biostatistical support to determine adequate sample size and appropriate statistical analysis, iii) assessment of body composition by using dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) and energy expenditure by using indirect calorimetry, iv) assistance in developing and preparing study-specific meals for metabolic testing and take-out meals for diet intervention studies, v) stable isotopically labeled metabolic tracer and hormone infusates to assess metabolic function, vi) subsidized clinical laboratory tests to determine participant eligibility and evaluate metabolic functions, vii) a trained research nurse practitioner to obtain muscle and adipose tissue biopsy samples, insert radial artery catheters for blood sampling, and assess vascular function, viii) cardiopulmonary fitness [VO2 peak], strength and physical performance testing, ix) assistance in implementing lifestyle interventions (behavioral education for weight loss and exercise training); and x) training in specific procedures to aid investigators in the performance of clinical studies. The Metabolic Kinetics sub-core assists investigators by providing: i) consultation in designing protocols to evaluate metabolic kinetics (e.g., the hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp procedure in conjunction with stable isotopically-labeled tracer infusions, frequently sampled intravenous glucose tolerance test and the modified 3-hour oral glucose tolerance test to evaluate whole-body and tissue- -cell function) and in interpreting the results of the data generated by core analyses, ii) assessment of substrate kinetics (e.g. endogenous glucose production rate, glucose disposal rate, lipolytic rate, protein synthesis, de novo lipogenesis, VLDL-triglyceride and apolipoprotein B-100 production and clearance rates) and “dynamic metabolomics” to evaluate metabolite flux through entire metabolic networks.by using mass-spectrometry to determine tracer enrichment of metabolic substrates and macromolecules, iii) mathematical modeling of tracer and non-tracer data to assess metabolic kinetics, iv) plasma and tissue metabolomics, and lipidomics and plasma proteomics; and v) education and training in specific analyses and mathematical modeling approaches used to assess metabolic function.

title: A  Schizophrenia Extension Study for the NKI Rockland Sample II project: An Open Resource of Multimodal Brain, Physiology & Behavior from a Community Lifespan Sample
text:
Schizophrenia is a major neuropsychiatric disorder associated with long-term disability and excess mortality.
Large-scale brain imaging data sets capable of addressing the underlying causes and identifying novel
treatment approaches are lacking. This study leverages the ongoing NKI Rockland Sample II study to collect a
large-scale multimodal imaging data set in schizophrenia which will be shared on-line to allow open
investigation into causes and consequences of brain imaging abnormalities in schizophrenia.

title: Investigating nerve fiber-associated macrophages in prostate development
text:
In the prostate, an increased abundance of macrophages is associated with progression of prostate disease,
yet the function of macrophages in the prostate is poorly understood. Macrophages in the prostate were found
in association with nerve fibers; thus the proposed research will elucidate fundamental knowledge about the
role of macrophages on nerve fibers in the prostate, and how their interaction affects prostate growth during
development. Completion of this project will provide necessary training in critical analysis and scientific
communication to prepare the candidate for an independent research career.

title: Precision Apheresis: stem cell isolation from patients with sickle cell disease for gene therapy using high-throughput microfluidics
text:
Hematopoietic gene therapy has emerged as a transformative disease-modifying option for Sickle Cell Disease.
Obtaining a sufficient dose of peripheral blood stem cells is paramount to the success of gene therapy. This
proposal outlines an efficient microfluidic technology for stem cell isolation from patients with sickle cell disease.

title: Demonstrating safety and combination therapy potential of a novel nanoparticle delivery system
text:
The proposed research is most relevant to public health as these studies will generate new fundamental
knowledge in the development of a safe, efficacious and novel cancer immunotherapy and will advance one
promising therapy in preparation for clinical trials. The SMP nanoparticle formulation will improve the
transformation of “cold” into “hot” tumors by prolonging stimulation of the STING pathway leading to a robust
immune response in the tumor microenvironment. This approach may be efficacious as a monotherapy in some
cancers and will also augment the activity of other immunotherapies, particularly immune checkpoint inhibitors.

title: Structure-function studies of LAG3 interactions with antibodies and cellular ligands
text:
In this R01 proposal, we determine the immune checkpoint receptor LAG3 regulates T cell function. We will use
structural biology to visualize interactions between LAG3 and its ligands MHC class II and FGL1, and we will
develop a diverse antibody-based toolkit for studying melanoma responses to LAG3 immunotherapy.
Collectively, this research will inform the design of maximally effective LAG3-based cancer immunotherapies.

title: Mechanisms of accelerated calcification and structural degeneration of implantable biomaterials in pediatric cardiac surgery
text:
The goal of this application is to improve the durability of pediatric medical devices made of implantable
biomaterials thus reducing the need for multiple cardiac re-operations in children. Our lab discovered that the
permanent incorporation of circulating proteins via glycation can impair the structure of the biomaterials and
favor the absorption of calcium-binding proteins. Since glycation and calcification precursors are overexpressed
in children, we believe that our strategies to mitigate protein absorption will be particularly efficient in pediatric
patients.

title: Identification of approved drugs for BDNF insufficiency
text:
Discoveries from this research project could be quickly translated to therapeutic applications for a subset of
WAGR patients with BDNF haploinsufficiency. Due to the potent activity of BDNF in promoting neuronal survival,
repairing damaged synapses, and modulating synaptic transmission, the drug could also be used in combination
therapy for neurodegenerative diseases, major depressive disorder, and Rett syndrome.

title: Research Training Program in Behavioral and Biomedical Sciences
text: The Research Training Program in Behavioral and Biomedical Sciences (BBS) at West Virginia University prepares scientists for successful careers conducting research across scientific disciplines. Trainees learn transferable skills needed to address significant public health issues related to human behavior or behavioral risk factors for disease. Training focus areas include addiction, neuropsychiatric and neurological illnesses, cancer, stress, and aging, all of which represent major societal burdens in West Virginia and the broader Appalachian region.

title: Combination metabolic therapy for diffuse midline glioma
text:
Diffuse midline gliomas (DMGs) are deadly brain tumors in children. Our studies have identified a unique
combination of metabolic vulnerabilities that can be exploited for therapy and for visualizing early response to
therapy in DMGs. Clinical translation of our studies has the potential to improve outcomes and quality of life for
children with this pernicious form of cancer.

title: Suicide Transmission Dynamics on Social Media: Modeling Risk, Understanding Platform Differences, and Exploring Ethical Implications Among Young Adults
text:
This research project investigates the dynamic transmission of suicidal thoughts and behaviors among young
adults (18-25 years) on social media, focusing on Twitter/X and Reddit. Using a multi-method approach
integrating computational social science, natural language processing, dynamic social network analysis, and
ecological momentary assessment, the study aims to model suicide transmission in real time, identify modifiable
risk factors, and understand platform-specific influences on the spread of suicidal content. The findings will inform
the development of data-driven, ethically grounded, and scalable interventions to mitigate suicide risk among
young adults on social media

title: Structural requirements for sterol 14α-demethylases
text:
Integrating cryo-EM techniques into the P450 field will open new horizons in understanding
molecular dynamics and evolution (with the prospect of rational reprogramming) of this catalyst,
including its interactions with the electron donor partner proteins and biological membranes. For
CYP51 in particular, such knowledge is essential in developing new therapeutics that benefit human
health, in addressing the escalating problem of drug resistance in the clinic and will help validate the
proximal P450 surface as a new target for inhibition.

title: Metabolic aberrant stem cell and niche inflammation in obese and non-obese EO-CRC
text:
Early-onset colorectal cancer (EO-CRC) is rising alarmingly in younger adults and exhibits distinct biology
compared with late-onset CRC. This project—proposed as a new research direction—will establish a translatable
mechanistic model to define how diet- and obesity-related inflammation drives metabolic reprogramming that
accelerates cancer development. The findings will identify diet-responsive metabolic pathways as new
biomarkers and therapeutic targets that can be leveraged to prevent or reverse inflammation-associated EO-
CRC.

title: Development of multiplexed nanoscopy for ultrastructural phenotyping of retinal tissue
text:
Understanding the intricate spatial architecture of retinal tissues and cells at size scales ranging
from the cellular to the molecular level is vital for public health, offering deep insights into the
cellular processes disrupted in vision and vision-related diseases. In this project, we will develop
pan-OptiX, the first 3D multi-resolution and multi-color spatial proteomics technology and test it
with mouse retina tissue to help elucidate the 3D cellular networks and nanoscale signatures
associated with vision and vision-related disorders.

title: Novel gene regulatory networks underlying two specialized modes of craniofacial development in a new model system of pupfishes
text:
The spatial and temporal coordination of gene transcription is crucial to ensure that fundamental biological
processes, such as embryonic development, are successfully orchestrated, thereby allowing for the normal
functioning of an organism. By leveraging an endemic group of pupfishes from the Bahamas, which exhibit
extremely divergent craniofacial morphologies, I propose a multi-omics approach to unravel and functionally test
the gene networks and regulatory regions of the genome controlling changes in gene expression underlying their
naturally divergent craniofacial development.

title: Targeting inflammatory RAS-mutated AML leukemia stem cells
text:
RAS pathway mutations have recently emerged as a major driver of resistance in acute myeloid leukemia in the
era of newer targeted therapies, including the BCL2, FLT3 and IDH1/2 inhibitors. While RAS inhibitors with strong
preclinical evidence of efficacy are currently in clinical testing in solid tumors and are expected to be available in
the near future, issues related to toxicity and/or resistance may limit their efficacy. In this proposal, we will build
upon our recent work on unique properties of RAS-mutant leukemia stem cells, to identify and test new
therapeutic targets, specific to RAS-mutant acute myeloid leukemia stem cells.

title: Understanding the role of ubiquitination-like processes in bacterial antiviral immunity
text:
Human innate immune pathways are vital for defense against viruses. Mechanistic details regarding the role of
ubiquitin-like conjugation in these pathways (e.g. cGAS-STING and ISG15) are not fully understood, but we can
glean insights into these missing details through an understanding of bacterial antiphage systems that use similar
ubiquitination-like pathways to confer defense. Here, I will explore the mechanisms of ubiquitin-like conjugation
in bacterial phage defense, with the goal of improving our understanding of the evolution of ubiquitination in
immune signaling, and to inform the design of therapeutics that can modulate the cGAS-STING and ISG15
pathways in humans.

title: Targeting the ERK Pathway in RAS - and BRAF-Driven Lung Cancers
text:
Our project is focused on the development of therapies for lung cancers dependent on mutations in the KRAS
or RAF genes which together, account for approximately of 40% of these cancers and for a large portion of
several other cancers, all of which are difficult to treat. In our previous work, we have made significant strides in
understanding the biology of these tumors and developing inhibitors of RAF and KRAS for their treatment. We
now plan, in collaboration with other members of the P01, to build on this knowledge to develop effective
therapies for lung cancers with these mutations.

title: The role of cancer in cardiovascular disease
text:
Cancer and cardiovascular disease claim more lives than all other diseases, combined. Long considered
separate entities, emerging data suggest they may interact and even directly promote one another. Defining
their shared biology – and how to target it – could lead to new therapies for the world’s two leading killers.

title: Towards Precision Medicine for Thoracic Aortic Disease: Defining the Clinical and Genomic Drivers of Bicuspid Aortopathy
text:
This proposal will investigate the causative clinical factors, demographic variables, and genomic variants
associated with bicuspid aortic valve aortopathy, a heritable condition with poorly understood pathogenesis. The
proposal will use artificial intelligence methods of predictive modeling to discover clinical and demographic
variables associated with BAV aortopathy as well as whole genome sequencing analysis to define the drivers of
this complex disease. Successful completion of this study will allow development of precision medicine tools to
predict aortic disease risk at the individual patient level.
